tasks.title: Audit Existing Case Studies for Quality and Deployment Readiness
tasks.description: Perform a comprehensive audit of all existing case studies to identify strengths, weaknesses, and immediate fixes needed before deployment.
tasks.details:
1. Review all integrated case studies against the 8-phase template for completeness and consistency.
2. Create a structured audit document with the following sections:
   - Content completeness (missing sections, incomplete information)
   - Visual consistency (image quality, layout issues, responsive breakpoints)
   - Technical issues (broken links, loading problems, console errors)
   - UX concerns (navigation flow, readability, accessibility)
3. Prioritize issues as "Critical" (blocking deployment), "Important" (should fix before launch), or "Future Enhancement".
4. Document specific examples of what's working well to maintain in other case studies.
5. For critical issues, provide specific recommendations for fixes with code snippets or design adjustments where applicable.
6. Check image optimization status across all case studies (file size, format, responsive variants).
7. Verify that all case studies follow the established CSS patterns and don't introduce new inconsistencies.
8. Ensure all case studies are properly linked from the dropdown menu and navigation system.
9. Create a summary report highlighting patterns of issues that might affect multiple case studies.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Create a comprehensive checklist covering all audit criteria (content, visuals, technical, UX).
2. Manually review each case study against this checklist, documenting findings in the audit document.
3. Use browser developer tools to identify console errors, network issues, or performance problems.
4. Test each case study on at least 3 different viewport sizes to verify responsive behavior.
5. Run automated accessibility checks using tools like axe or Lighthouse.
6. Validate that all links within case studies work correctly.
7. Measure and document load times for each case study page.
8. Have a peer review the audit findings to ensure nothing was missed.
9. Create a prioritized list of fixes based on severity and impact on deployment readiness.
10. Verify that the audit document provides clear, actionable information for implementing fixes.

tasks.title: Fix Critical Navigation and Link Issues for Case Studies
tasks.description: Identify and resolve all navigation and link issues to ensure all case studies are accessible, properly connected, and maintain professional presentation.
tasks.details:
1. Conduct a comprehensive audit of all navigation elements leading to case studies:
   - Verify dropdown menu functionality and completeness
   - Check main navigation links to case study sections
   - Validate breadcrumb navigation within case studies
   - Ensure "Next Project" and "Previous Project" links work correctly

2. Fix identified issues:
   - Repair any broken or incorrect links in main navigation
   - Ensure all case studies listed in dropdown menus are properly linked
   - Implement consistent navigation patterns across all case studies
   - Add missing links to any case studies not currently accessible
   - Verify that all links use proper relative paths that will work in production

3. Implement navigation improvements:
   - Add "Back to Portfolio" links at appropriate locations
   - Ensure case study navigation follows logical progression
   - Implement smooth scrolling for in-page navigation
   - Add visual indicators for current page/section in navigation

4. Technical implementation:
   - Use consistent URL structure for all case studies
   - Implement proper event tracking for navigation analytics
   - Ensure all links have appropriate hover/focus states
   - Test navigation with keyboard-only interaction

5. Documentation:
   - Document the navigation structure and linking patterns
   - Create a site map showing all case study connections
   - Note any special considerations for future case study additions
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Automated testing:
   - Run automated link checkers to identify broken links
   - Use Cypress or Playwright to test navigation paths to all case studies
   - Verify that all case studies are reachable from multiple entry points

2. Manual testing:
   - Perform systematic click-through testing of all navigation elements
   - Test dropdown menus on desktop and mobile devices
   - Verify that breadcrumb navigation accurately reflects site hierarchy
   - Test keyboard navigation for all links and dropdown menus
   - Validate that "Next/Previous" navigation follows logical sequence

3. Cross-browser and device testing:
   - Test navigation on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge
   - Verify mobile navigation works correctly on iOS and Android devices
   - Test tablet view navigation and touch interactions

4. Accessibility validation:
   - Verify all navigation elements are keyboard accessible
   - Confirm proper ARIA attributes on navigation components
   - Test with screen readers to ensure navigation is properly announced

5. Documentation validation:
   - Cross-reference site map with actual implementation
   - Verify all case studies appear in navigation as expected

tasks.title: Verify Netlify Deployment Quality and Finalize for Deadline
tasks.description: Perform final verification of the Netlify deployment to ensure professional presentation quality and make any last-minute adjustments before the midnight deadline.
tasks.details:
1. Access the live Netlify deployment and conduct a comprehensive verification:
   - Verify all pages load correctly with proper styling and assets
   - Check for any console errors or network issues
   - Test all interactive elements (navigation, dropdowns, forms)
   - Validate mobile responsiveness on key breakpoints (320px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px)
   - Confirm all case studies are accessible and properly formatted
   - Verify load times are optimized (target < 3s on desktop, < 5s on mobile)

2. Address any critical issues found:
   - Prioritize fixes based on visibility and impact on professional presentation
   - Make direct changes in the Netlify dashboard for quick CSS fixes if needed
   - For more complex issues, implement fixes in the codebase and trigger a new deployment

3. Optimize Netlify settings:
   - Enable asset optimization (CSS/JS minification, image compression)
   - Configure proper caching headers
   - Verify custom domain and SSL settings
   - Enable Netlify's built-in analytics for post-launch monitoring

4. Document deployment status:
   - Create a final deployment report noting any known issues and their severity
   - Document any environment-specific configurations or workarounds
   - Record performance metrics as a baseline for future reference

5. Prepare communication for stakeholders:
   - Draft a brief status update confirming deployment completion
   - Include the live URL and any important notes about the deployment
   - Note any known limitations or planned future improvements
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Automated verification:
   - Run Lighthouse tests on key pages (homepage, case study template, contact)
   - Use axe or similar tools to verify accessibility compliance
   - Check for broken links using automated tools
   - Verify proper meta tags and SEO elements

2. Manual testing checklist:
   - Verify all navigation paths and links work correctly
   - Test all case studies for proper formatting and content display
   - Check responsive behavior on multiple devices (or device simulators)
   - Verify all images load correctly and are properly optimized
   - Test contact form functionality if applicable
   - Verify social media links direct to correct profiles

3. Cross-browser verification:
   - Test on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge
   - Verify consistent presentation across browsers
   - Document any browser-specific issues and their severity

4. Performance validation:
   - Measure and document page load times
   - Verify Time to Interactive metrics
   - Check for any render-blocking resources
   - Validate image optimization

5. Final approval process:
   - Conduct a final walkthrough with stakeholder(s) if possible
   - Document any feedback received
   - Confirm the site meets professional presentation standards
   - Get explicit sign-off on deployment quality
